We are working on a yaml config file structure for our in development "Model Independent Emissions Module" (MIEM) within the MUSICA ecosystem.  The primary constraint is that it fits any existing mechanism/config for MICM (e.g. matching the style, etc.). Part of this task is determining what is already in the MICM config, since MIEM will need to reference that to determine the species that are being emitted. I will include the raw notes (which have things that can be ignored, such as specific peoples names, etc). Parse these, identify only the information that is relevant to our task here, and generate a preliminary yaml config file design for MIEM that meets the stated section priorities. : """Draft MIEM Config file structure

Anthropogenic emissions section





Input data directory



Filename structure



Species list



Process different sectors (True/False)



Do VOC speciation (True/False)





If VOC speciation is True, define how to do it? Maybe, ask Claire/Louisa how it is done in CAMS and replicate the same method in MIEM. We will need the sector information for VOC speciation. 



Apply climatological diurnal variation to global emissions (True/False)





Use Olivier et al., (2003) (This is likely used in CAMS-TEMPO) as a starting point for different sectors. Control profiles through config file. 



Have two options





One profile per sector for entire globe



Regionally varying sector-wise diurnal profile (wishlist, not a priority right now)



Vertical distribution of point sources (True/False)





Need to look into how to constrain this. We have information about the US from NEI but not sure about the rest of the world.



Someone could run SMOKE over any part of the world and get this information but running SMOKE would be a heavy lift. 



Provide an example format for vertically distributing the emissions. Look at EPA_ANTHRO_EMIS to see how it is done for NEI -> WRF-Chem mapping. 



Combine emission inventories (True/False, e.g., CAMS + NEI)





Define locations of emission inventories to be combined 



Do different datasets have the same species? If not, then do the mapping. 



Bring Haipeng Lin into one of our meetings to see what is being done with HEMCO.  

Biomass Burning Section





Input data directory



Filename structure 



Species list



Do VOC speciation (True/False)





If VOC speciation is True, define how to do it? Maybe, use the speciation FINN uses for different mechanisms. 



Discuss with Louisa and maybe Kelly Barsanti if we can bring NEIVA for this purpose? Louisa has done it for FINN 2.6 but using NEIVA is not straightforward. 



Can potentially use standard emissions ratios from FINN and apply those to different emission inventories (Need to think about it). 



Identify emitted species from MICM config yaml file. 



Apply climatological diurnal variation to emissions (True/False)





Replicate UPTEMPO. Define hourly factors in the config file itself so that end users can change those here itself.



Build an option to allow end users to override climatological diurnal variation with local data (e.g. Thailand specific diurnal variation)



Vertical distribution of fire emissions





We probably don’t need this as a config file option and can always read in parameters required for plumerise calculation.



Provide options to read-in 3D biomass burning files if someone runs the plumerise offline. 



QUACS can enable users to implement their own plumerise parametrization. 

Biogenic emissions - offline or online





If they are offline, they can be read similar to anthropogenic emissions. 



Online emissions 





MEGAN code will sit outside MIEM. MIEM will only get emission fluxes from MEGAN and other online emission modules and pass those to the solvers.  



Should MIEM handle necessary input datasets for MEGAN? 



Can we leverage land use information from the static geographical fields rather than reading those separately from MODIS?

Dust emissions - online





Interface with QUACS to allow users to use their own parameterization. This code will sit outside MIEM and MIEM will only get emission fluxes from dust emission schemes and pass those to the solvers. 

Sea-salt emissions - online 





Interface with QUACS to allow users to use their own parameterization. This code will sit outside MIEM and MIEM will only get emission fluxes from sea-salt emission schemes and pass those to the solvers. 





Lightning NOx emissions - online





Interface with QUACS to allow users to use their own parameterization. This code will sit outside MIEM and MIEM will only get emission fluxes from lightning NOx emission schemes and pass those to the solvers. """



I also have the following personal notes I took from a recent meeting: """HEMCO

https://github.com/ESCOMP/HEMCO_CESM

TODO:





Make an initial YAML config structure



Goal make sure Kyle approves it and it is model independent





Questions





Do we want this all in the MICM file, or just have the MICM config point to the controlling configuration file for MIEM?





Does MICM use these values also?



Would this tool benefit from a WASM or other straightforward GUI to allow for selection/addition of sources, species, sectors, etc.





This might be what QUACS will be



Perhaps we add a feature that reads the MICM file to determine the species to generate the MIEM configuration file





Or it could be a GUI tool (preferred)



Look at musicbox website: https://musicbox.acom.ucar.edu/



How would QUACS integrate?

Notes





In a miem config file





Different sections for:





Anthropogenic



Biomass Burning 



Biogenic (offline / online)



Dust (online)



Sea-salt (online)



Lightning NOx emissions (online)



Try to dig into what the requirements might be to get info from e.g. CAMS-TEMPO



Wrf-chem preprocessing tools may be useful to look at



1. MIEM should read the MICM config and determine the species that are being emitted



2. MIEM needs to figure out the mapping to the MICM species

Anthropogenic:





Some inventories of VOC (volatile organic compound)





Need species list



Need sectors list



FINN has a tool (for biomass burning and VOCs) that might be applied to Anthropogenic emissions as well

Biogenic:





Offline would be similar to anthro



Online – MEGAN code will set outside MIEM and only moderate emissions rate





Eventually bring it in through QUACS



Only one way (most common way) to calculate Biogenic





Online Modules





Code will sit outside MIEM



MIEM will only get emission fluxes from {type} emission schemes and pass those to the solvers

Most helpful from user perspective





User provides their KPP file, it recognized the species, has a mapping (or informs that none exists and requires user input)"""

input.prompt:
In /Users/vweeks/NCAR/ACOM/CheMPAS/MIEM, I need to know what MIEM configuration patterns already exist so I can design a YAML config without duplicating or conflicting with what's there.

Please find and summarize:

1. docs/ses-1.0.md — summarize the SES convention (dimensions, attributes, key fields) briefly.
2. Any existing config-loading code in src/ and include/miem/ — search for yaml-cpp / YAML::Node / LoadFile. Identify the config schema currently supported (top-level keys, expected fields).
3. Look for files named like miem*.yaml, config*.yaml, example*.yaml in test/data/, examples/, docs/.
4. What sections/knobs the current code already expects (input dir, filenames, species lists, scaling, sector labels, category/hierarchy aggregation, diurnal, VOC speciation, vertical distribution, inventory combining).
5. How species mapping to MICM is currently handled (if at all) — grep for "species", "QuerySpecies", "ResolveHostIndices", "mapping".

Report with exact file paths and short excerpts of key config fields. Under 400 words.

content.text:
Excellent. Let me gather a summary now with a final check on any other pattern details:

## Summary: MIEM Configuration Patterns

**1. SES Convention (ses-1.0.md)**
- **Dimensions**: `n_cells` (spatial, host-grid-aligned), `time` (unlimited)
- **Global Attributes**: `ses_version="1.0"`, `Conventions="CF-1.8"`, `grid_description`, `source_inventory`, `preprocessing_tool_version`
- **Emission Variables**: `emi_<species>(time, n_cells)` with units `kg m-2 s-1`

**2. Config Loading (include/miem/config.hpp + src/config.cpp)**
Top-level YAML key: **`miem`**
- `version`: string (default "1.0")
- `sources`: sequence of SourceConfig objects

Per-source fields:
- `name`: source identifier
- `type`: "anthropogenic", "fire", "biogenic", "offline"
- `file_pattern`: file path with optional `{YYYY}{MM}{DD}` tokens
- `species_map`: path to species mapping YAML
- `temporal_interpolation`: "linear" (default) or "nearest"
- `vertical_injection`: "surface" (default) or other levels
- `descriptor`: optional, for non-SES files
- `category`: int (grouping for aggregation)
- `hierarchy`: int (priority within category; higher wins)
- `sector`: string label for diagnostics
- `scaling_factor`: float (runtime multiplicative scaling)

**3. Existing Config Files**
- `/Users/vweeks/NCAR/ACOM/CheMPAS/MIEM/configs/example_miem.yaml` — two sources (CAMS anthropogenic, FINN fire)
- `/Users/vweeks/NCAR/ACOM/CheMPAS/MIEM/configs/example_species_map.yaml` — mechanism "MOZART-T1", mappings with scaling
- `/Users/vweeks/NCAR/ACOM/CheMPAS/MIEM/configs/example_descriptor.yaml` — non-SES file descriptor
- `/Users/vweeks/NCAR/ACOM/CheMPAS/MIEM/test/data/test_config.yaml` — minimal test config

**4. Species Mapping (include/miem/species_map.hpp)**
YAML structure:
```yaml
species_map:
  mechanism: "MOZART-T1"
  mappings:
    - inventory: "NOx"
      mechanism: "NO"
      scaling: 0.9
```
Each mapping: `inventory_name → mechanism_name` with optional `scaling_factor`. Multiple mechanisms supported; `Apply()` accumulates fluxes into mechanism species.

**5. Dataset Descriptor (include/miem/dataset_descriptor.hpp)**
For non-SES files:
- `variable_prefix`: default "emi_"
- `flux_units`: default "kg m-2 s-1"
- `unit_conversion_factor`: 1.0 by default
- `time_dimension`, `cell_dimension`: dimension names
- `species_rename`: map original var names to canonical SES names

**6. Species Handling**
- `EmissionsModule::QuerySpecies(config_path)` — returns merged mechanism species list across all sources
- `EmissionsModule::ResolveHostIndices()` — maps host model species names to MIEM indices
- `OfflineEmissionSource::QuerySpecies()` — per-source species list
- `SESReader::QuerySpecies()` — extracts `emi_*` variable names from input files

No aggregation/hierarchy logic in current config schema—handled internally by category/hierarchy fields during `Update()` calls.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
MICM uses the CAMP convention: a top-level `camp-files:` list that includes other YAML/JSON files, each containing a `camp-data:` array of typed entries (`type: CHEM_SPEC`, `type: MECHANISM`, etc.). It's a flat, declarative, include-based schema — JSON and YAML are interchangeable.

The existing MIEM config (`configs/example_miem.yaml`) uses a different top-level key `miem:` with a `sources:` list — stylistically adjacent to CAMP but not CAMP-native. The design question is whether to adopt `camp-data` typing (e.g. `type: EMISSIONS_SOURCE`) so MIEM configs can live alongside MICM configs, or keep the current `miem:` namespace and have MICM point to it by reference.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Now I'll write the plan.

input.content:
# MIEM YAML Config Structure — Preliminary Design

## Context

MIEM (Model Independent Emissions Module) needs a YAML configuration format that:

1. **Matches MICM's stylistic conventions** so both configs feel native within the MUSICA ecosystem.
2. **References the MICM config** to discover the set of chemical species the host mechanism requires, then maps inventory species → mechanism species.
3. **Covers all emission source categories** from the user's draft notes: anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (offline/online), dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx. Anthropogenic and biomass burning are the highest-priority sections; online modules (dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx, online biogenic/MEGAN) are interface-only — MIEM receives fluxes rather than computing them.

The existing MIEM scaffolding already supports a subset of this (`configs/example_miem.yaml` with a `miem:` namespace, sources with `type`, `file_pattern`, `species_map`, category/hierarchy aggregation, per-source `scaling_factor`). The new design extends that scaffolding to cover the full v1 feature set while aligning with CAMP-style conventions used by MICM.

## Reference: MICM (CAMP) Config Style

From `NCAR/micm` (`test/tutorial/configs/rate_constants_no_user_defined/`):

```yaml
# config.yaml — include-based entry point
camp-files:
  - species.yaml
  - reactions.yaml
```

```yaml
# species.yaml — typed, flat list of entries
camp-data:
  - name: "NO"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
    molecular weight [kg mol-1]: 0.030
  - name: "ISOP"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
```

Key stylistic traits to adopt:

- Top-level `camp-files:` as an include manifest (MIEM can add `miem-files:` analog, or reuse the same pattern).
- Entries live in a `camp-data:` array, each with `name:` and `type:` and arbitrary typed fields.
- Units embedded in key names using square brackets (`molecular weight [kg mol-1]`).
- YAML and JSON are interchangeable.

## Design Decision: MIEM as a Parallel Manifest

**Recommendation:** Keep MIEM's configuration in its **own top-level manifest file** (not inlined into the MICM config), but have the MIEM manifest carry a `micm_config:` reference so MIEM can parse MICM's species list at load time.

Rationale:
- Keeps the MICM file purely a chemistry description — usable standalone by MusicBox and other clients that don't need emissions.
- Matches the meeting-note preference ("Or it could be a GUI tool [QUACS] that reads the MICM file to generate the MIEM config").
- Avoids schema drift: MICM stays CAMP-pure; MIEM declares its own `miem-data` typed entries in the same style.

## Preliminary YAML Design

### 1. Top-level manifest (`miem.yaml`)

```yaml
miem:
  version: "1.0"

  # Points to the MICM/CAMP config so MIEM can query the mechanism species list.
  # MIEM reads this at startup to (a) know which species it must provide fluxes for,
  # and (b) validate that every mapping target exists in the mechanism.
  micm_config: "./mechanism/config.yaml"
  mechanism_name: "MOZART-T1"   # informational; cross-checked against MICM file

  # Include manifest, CAMP-style. Each included file contributes miem-data entries.
  miem-files:
    - sources/anthropogenic.yaml
    - sources/biomass_burning.yaml
    - sources/biogenic.yaml
    - online_interfaces.yaml
    - species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml
    - species_maps/finn_to_mozart.yaml
```

### 2. Anthropogenic section (`sources/anthropogenic.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "cams_global_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"

    # I/O
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../cams-v6.2"
    file_pattern: "CAMS-GLOB-ANT_v6.2_{YYYY}{MM}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"            # or "custom" → requires descriptor:
    # descriptor: { variable_prefix: "emi_", flux_units: "kg m-2 s-1", ... }

    # Species
    species: ["NO", "NO2", "CO", "SO2", "NH3", "VOC_total"]
    species_map: "cams_to_mozart"    # references a SPECIES_MAP entry by name

    # Sectors & aggregation (HEMCO-style)
    process_sectors: true
    sectors: ["energy", "industry", "transport", "residential", "agriculture"]
    category: 1
    hierarchy: 1
    scaling_factor: 1.0

    # VOC speciation
    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "cams_tempo"            # or "finn_ratios", "custom"
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/cams_tempo_by_sector.yaml"

# MIEM YAML Config Structure — Preliminary Design

## Context

MIEM (Model Independent Emissions Module) needs a YAML configuration format that:

1. **Matches MICM's stylistic conventions** so both configs feel native within the MUSICA ecosystem.
2. **References the MICM config** to discover the set of chemical species the host mechanism requires, then maps inventory species → mechanism species.
3. **Covers all emission source categories** from the user's draft notes: anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (offline/online), dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx. Anthropogenic and biomass burning are the highest-priority sections; online modules (dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx, online biogenic/MEGAN) are interface-only — MIEM receives fluxes rather than computing them.

The existing MIEM scaffolding already supports a subset of this (`configs/example_miem.yaml` with a `miem:` namespace, sources with `type`, `file_pattern`, `species_map`, category/hierarchy aggregation, per-source `scaling_factor`). The new design extends that scaffolding to cover the full v1 feature set while aligning with CAMP-style conventions used by MICM.

## Reference: MICM (CAMP) Config Style

From `NCAR/micm` (`test/tutorial/configs/rate_constants_no_user_defined/`):

```yaml
# config.yaml — include-based entry point
camp-files:
  - species.yaml
  - reactions.yaml
```

```yaml
# species.yaml — typed, flat list of entries
camp-data:
  - name: "NO"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
    molecular weight [kg mol-1]: 0.030
  - name: "ISOP"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
```

Key stylistic traits to adopt:

- Top-level `camp-files:` as an include manifest (MIEM can add `miem-files:` analog, or reuse the same pattern).
- Entries live in a `camp-data:` array, each with `name:` and `type:` and arbitrary typed fields.
- Units embedded in key names using square brackets (`molecular weight [kg mol-1]`).
- YAML and JSON are interchangeable.

## Design Decision: MIEM as a Parallel Manifest

**Recommendation:** Keep MIEM's configuration in its **own top-level manifest file** (not inlined into the MICM config), but have the MIEM manifest carry a `micm_config:` reference so MIEM can parse MICM's species list at load time.

Rationale:
- Keeps the MICM file purely a chemistry description — usable standalone by MusicBox and other clients that don't need emissions.
- Matches the meeting-note preference ("Or it could be a GUI tool [QUACS] that reads the MICM file to generate the MIEM config").
- Avoids schema drift: MICM stays CAMP-pure; MIEM declares its own `miem-data` typed entries in the same style.

## Preliminary YAML Design

### 1. Top-level manifest (`miem.yaml`)

```yaml

  version: "1.0"

  # MIEM reads this at startup to (a) know which species it must provide fluxes for,
  # and (b) validate that every mapping target exists in the mechanism.
  micm_config: "./mechanism/config.yaml"
  mechanism_name: "MOZART-T1"   # informational; cross-checked against MICM file

  # Include manifest, CAMP-style. Each included file contributes miem-data entries.
  miem-files:
    - sources/anthropogenic.yaml
    - sources/biomass_burning.yaml
    - sources/biogenic.yaml
    - online_interfaces.yaml
    - species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml
    - species_maps/finn_to_mozart.yaml

### 2. Anthropogenic section (`sources/anthropogenic.yaml`) — Priority 1

    species_map: "cams_to_mozart"    # references a SPECIES_MAP entry by name

    category: 1
    hierarchy: 1

1. **Matches MICM's stylistic conventions** so both configs feel native within the MUSICA ecosystem.
2. **References the MICM config** to discover the set of chemical species the host mechanism requires, then maps inventory species → mechanism species.
3. **Covers all emission source categories** from the user's draft notes: anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (offline/online), dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx. Anthropogenic and biomass burning are the highest-priority sections; online modules (dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx, online biogenic/MEGAN) are interface-only — MIEM receives fluxes rather than computing them.

The existing MIEM scaffolding already supports a subset of this (`configs/example_miem.yaml` with a `miem:` namespace, sources with `type`, `file_pattern`, `species_map`, category/hierarchy aggregation, per-source `scaling_factor`). The new design extends that scaffolding to cover the full v1 feature set while aligning with CAMP-style conventions used by MICM.

## Reference: MICM (CAMP) Config Style

From `NCAR/micm` (`test/tutorial/configs/rate_constants_no_user_defined/`):

```yaml
# config.yaml — include-based entry point
camp-files:
  - species.yaml
  - reactions.yaml
```

```yaml
# species.yaml — typed, flat list of entries
camp-data:
  - name: "NO"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
    molecular weight [kg mol-1]: 0.030
  - name: "ISOP"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
```

Key stylistic traits to adopt:

- Top-level `camp-files:` as an include manifest (MIEM can add `miem-files:` analog, or reuse the same pattern).
- Entries live in a `camp-data:` array, each with `name:` and `type:` and arbitrary typed fields.
- Units embedded in key names using square brackets (`molecular weight [kg mol-1]`).
- YAML and JSON are interchangeable.

## Design Decision: MIEM as a Parallel Manifest

**Recommendation:** Keep MIEM's configuration in its **own top-level manifest file** (not inlined into the MICM config), but have the MIEM manifest carry a `micm_config:` reference so MIEM can parse MICM's species list at load time.

Rationale:
- Keeps the MICM file purely a chemistry description — usable standalone by MusicBox and other clients that don't need emissions.
- Matches the meeting-note preference ("Or it could be a GUI tool [QUACS] that reads the MICM file to generate the MIEM config").
- Avoids schema drift: MICM stays CAMP-pure; MIEM declares its own `miem-data` typed entries in the same style.

## Preliminary YAML Design

### 1. Top-level manifest (`miem.yaml`)

```yaml
miem:
  version: "1.0"

  # Points to the MICM/CAMP config so MIEM can query the mechanism species list.
  # MIEM reads this at startup to (a) know which species it must provide fluxes for,
  # and (b) validate that every mapping target exists in the mechanism.
  micm_config: "./mechanism/config.yaml"
  mechanism_name: "MOZART-T1"   # informational; cross-checked against MICM file

  # Include manifest, CAMP-style. Each included file contributes miem-data entries.
  miem-files:
    - sources/anthropogenic.yaml
    - sources/biomass_burning.yaml
    - sources/biogenic.yaml
    - online_interfaces.yaml
    - species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml
    - species_maps/finn_to_mozart.yaml
```

### 2. Anthropogenic section (`sources/anthropogenic.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "cams_global_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"

    # I/O
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../cams-v6.2"
    file_pattern: "CAMS-GLOB-ANT_v6.2_{YYYY}{MM}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"            # or "custom" → requires descriptor:
    # descriptor: { variable_prefix: "emi_", flux_units: "kg m-2 s-1", ... }

    # Species
    species: ["NO", "NO2", "CO", "SO2", "NH3", "VOC_total"]
    species_map: "cams_to_mozart"    # references a SPECIES_MAP entry by name

    # Sectors & aggregation (HEMCO-style)
    process_sectors: true
    sectors: ["energy", "industry", "transport", "residential", "agriculture"]
    category: 1
    hierarchy: 1
    scaling_factor: 1.0

    # VOC speciation
    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "cams_tempo"            # or "finn_ratios", "custom"
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/cams_tempo_by_sector.yaml"
      # When enabled, per-sector speciation splits lumped VOC into mechanism species.

    # Diurnal variation
    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global_per_sector"       # or "regional_per_sector" (wishlist)
      profile_file: "diurnal/olivier_2003.yaml"   # 24 hourly factors per sector

    # Vertical distribution of point sources
    vertical_distribution:
      enabled: false
      # When enabled:
      # profile_file: "vertical/nei_point_sources.yaml"
      # fallback: "surface"           # used where profile is undefined

  # Inventory combining: declare a second source and let category/hierarchy
  # arbitrate overlap (higher hierarchy wins within the same category).
  - name: "nei_us_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../nei-2020"
    file_pattern: "NEI_2020_{YYYY}{MM}{DD}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"
    species_map: "nei_to_mozart"
    category: 1        # same category as CAMS → compared by hierarchy
    hierarchy: 2       # NEI wins over CAMS where both are defined (US domain)
    sectors: [...]
    # ... (same structure as above)
```

### 3. Biomass burning section (`sources/biomass_burning.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "finn_2.6"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "biomass_burning"

    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../finn-2.6"
    file_pattern: "FINN_{YYYY}{DDD}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"
    species: ["CO", "NO", "NMVOC", "PM2.5", ...]
    species_map: "finn_to_mozart"

    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "finn_ratios"            # FINN-native speciation by biome/fuel
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/finn_mozart_t1.yaml"
      # Future: method: "neiva" once integration exists.

    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global"                   # UPTEMPO-style single profile for fires
      profile_file: "diurnal/uptempo_fire.yaml"
      hourly_factors_inline:           # allow override inline (per notes)
        - [0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.15,
           0.14, 0.12, 0.09, 0.07, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02, 0.01,
           0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005]
      regional_override:
        enabled: false
        # file: "diurnal/thailand_local.nc"   # spatial mask + hourly factors

    vertical_distribution:
      mode: "online_plumerise"         # default — plumerise runs in-model
      # mode: "offline_3d"             # read precomputed 3D fire emissions
      # file_pattern: "FINN_3D_{YYYY}{DDD}.nc"
      # QUACS hook: users can swap in their own plumerise parameterization.
```

### 4. Biogenic (`sources/biogenic.yaml`) — offline *or* online

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "megan_online"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "biogenic"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "megan"                 # code lives outside MIEM (QUACS-managed)
    # MIEM only receives fluxes from this provider and forwards them.
    species_map: "megan_to_mozart"
    # Optional: whether MIEM should stage MEGAN input datasets:
    stage_inputs: false
    # If true: MIEM reads land-use from host static fields rather than MODIS.
    use_host_landuse: true

  # Alternative offline form — structurally identical to anthropogenic:
  # - name: "megan_offline_climo"
  #   type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
  #   category_type: "biogenic"
  #   mode: "offline"
  #   input_directory: ...
  #   file_pattern: ...
  #   species_map: ...
```

### 5. Online-only interface sources (`online_interfaces.yaml`)

Dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx — MIEM is a pass-through that collects fluxes computed by external (QUACS-managed) modules.

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "dust_online"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "dust"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.dust"            # QUACS-provided scheme name
    species_map: "dust_to_mozart"

  - name: "seasalt_online"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "sea_salt"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.seasalt"
    species_map: "seasalt_to_mozart"

  - name: "lightning_nox"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "lightning_nox"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.lightning"
    species_map: "lightning_to_mozart"
```

### 6. Species maps (`species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml`)

Reuses the existing `SpeciesMap` structure already present in the code
(`include/miem/species_map.hpp`), re-typed as a `miem-data` entry for consistency:

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "cams_to_mozart"
    type: "SPECIES_MAP"
    mechanism: "MOZART-T1"
    mappings:
      - inventory: "NOx"
        mechanism: "NO"
        scaling: 0.9
      - inventory: "NOx"
        mechanism: "NO2"
        scaling: 0.1
      - inventory: "CO"
        mechanism: "CO"

    # at load time — echoes the meeting note "informs that none exists and
    # requires user input".
```

### 7. Diurnal / VOC / vertical profile files

These are small standalone YAML files referenced by the source entries — also
`miem-data` typed, for include-compatibility:

```yaml
# diurnal/olivier_2003.yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "olivier_2003_diurnal"
    type: "DIURNAL_PROFILE"
    sectors:
      energy:       [0.03, 0.03, ...24 values]
      transport:    [0.01, 0.01, ...]
      residential:  [...]
```

## Critical Files to Modify (when implementation begins)

Design-only task now; listing for downstream work:

- `include/miem/config.hpp`, `src/config.cpp` — extend schema to accept `micm_config`, `miem-files`, typed `miem-data` entries, `voc_speciation`, `diurnal`, `vertical_distribution`, `mode`, `provider`, `category_type`.
- `include/miem/species_map.hpp` — already structurally adequate; re-type wrapping into `type: SPECIES_MAP`.
- `configs/example_miem.yaml` — migrate to the new schema as a worked example.
- `docs/` — add `miem-config-1.0.md` alongside `ses-1.0.md`.
- A new lightweight MICM config reader (just for species list extraction) — parse `camp-data` entries with `type: CHEM_SPEC`.

## Open Questions for the User

Per Phase 3, flagging decisions that should be confirmed before implementation:

1. **Embed vs. reference:** Plan recommends MIEM as a separate manifest that *references* the MICM config. Alternative is a single combined file with both `camp-data` and `miem-data` arrays. Confirm preference.
2. **`miem-files` vs reusing `camp-files`:** If the community wants a single include mechanism, MIEM entries could be carried inside `camp-files:` lists with distinct `type:` values. This lets MusicBox, QUACS, etc. use one loader. Tradeoff: MICM must ignore unknown types.
3. **VOC speciation method enum:** Current draft lists `cams_tempo`, `finn_ratios`, `custom`. Should `neiva` be a named method now as a forward-looking stub?
4. **Regional diurnal override format:** `profile_file` + optional `regional_override.file` (NetCDF mask) — or a single NetCDF that carries both default and regional? NEI/SMOKE compatibility may dictate.

## Verification

Design artifact only — no code to run. To validate the schema before implementation:

- Walk through `docs/ses-1.0.md` and confirm the `convention: "SES-1.0"` field maps cleanly to the existing `SESReader` detection logic.
- Hand-author a sample `miem.yaml` per this design, load it through a stub parser, and confirm every field has a home in the C++ `SourceConfig`/`SpeciesMap` structs (or an expansion thereof).
- Circulate with Kyle (per meeting notes: "Goal — make sure Kyle approves it and it is model independent") and Claire/Louisa for VOC speciation fields.

# MIEM YAML Config Structure — Preliminary Design

## Context

MIEM (Model Independent Emissions Module) needs a YAML configuration format that:

1. **Matches MICM's stylistic conventions** so both configs feel native within the MUSICA ecosystem.
2. **References the MICM config** to discover the set of chemical species the host mechanism requires, then maps inventory species → mechanism species.
3. **Covers all emission source categories** from the user's draft notes: anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (offline/online), dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx. Anthropogenic and biomass burning are the highest-priority sections; online modules (dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx, online biogenic/MEGAN) are interface-only — MIEM receives fluxes rather than computing them.

The existing MIEM scaffolding already supports a subset of this (`configs/example_miem.yaml` with a `miem:` namespace, sources with `type`, `file_pattern`, `species_map`, category/hierarchy aggregation, per-source `scaling_factor`). The new design extends that scaffolding to cover the full v1 feature set while aligning with CAMP-style conventions used by MICM.

## Reference: MICM (CAMP) Config Style

From `NCAR/micm` (`test/tutorial/configs/rate_constants_no_user_defined/`):

```yaml
# config.yaml — include-based entry point
camp-files:
  - species.yaml
  - reactions.yaml
```

```yaml
# species.yaml — typed, flat list of entries
camp-data:
  - name: "NO"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
    molecular weight [kg mol-1]: 0.030
  - name: "ISOP"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
```

Key stylistic traits to adopt:

- Top-level `camp-files:` as an include manifest (MIEM can add `miem-files:` analog, or reuse the same pattern).
- Entries live in a `camp-data:` array, each with `name:` and `type:` and arbitrary typed fields.
- Units embedded in key names using square brackets (`molecular weight [kg mol-1]`).
- YAML and JSON are interchangeable.

## Design Decision: MIEM as a Parallel Manifest

**Recommendation:** Keep MIEM's configuration in its **own top-level manifest file** (not inlined into the MICM config), but have the MIEM manifest carry a `micm_config:` reference so MIEM can parse MICM's species list at load time.

Rationale:
- Keeps the MICM file purely a chemistry description — usable standalone by MusicBox and other clients that don't need emissions.
- Matches the meeting-note preference ("Or it could be a GUI tool [QUACS] that reads the MICM file to generate the MIEM config").
- Avoids schema drift: MICM stays CAMP-pure; MIEM declares its own `miem-data` typed entries in the same style.

## Preliminary YAML Design

### 1. Top-level manifest (`miem.yaml`)

```yaml
miem:
  version: "1.0"

  # Points to the MICM/CAMP config so MIEM can query the mechanism species list.
  # MIEM reads this at startup to (a) know which species it must provide fluxes for,
  # and (b) validate that every mapping target exists in the mechanism.
  micm_config: "./mechanism/config.yaml"
  mechanism_name: "MOZART-T1"   # informational; cross-checked against MICM file

  # Include manifest, CAMP-style. Each included file contributes miem-data entries.
  miem-files:
    - sources/anthropogenic.yaml
    - sources/biomass_burning.yaml
    - sources/biogenic.yaml
    - online_interfaces.yaml
    - species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml
    - species_maps/finn_to_mozart.yaml
```

### 2. Anthropogenic section (`sources/anthropogenic.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "cams_global_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"

    # I/O
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../cams-v6.2"
    file_pattern: "CAMS-GLOB-ANT_v6.2_{YYYY}{MM}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"            # or "custom" → requires descriptor:
    # descriptor: { variable_prefix: "emi_", flux_units: "kg m-2 s-1", ... }

    # Species
    species: ["NO", "NO2", "CO", "SO2", "NH3", "VOC_total"]
    species_map: "cams_to_mozart"    # references a SPECIES_MAP entry by name

    # Sectors & aggregation (HEMCO-style)
    process_sectors: true
    sectors: ["energy", "industry", "transport", "residential", "agriculture"]
    category: 1
    hierarchy: 1
    scaling_factor: 1.0

    # VOC speciation
    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "cams_tempo"            # or "finn_ratios", "custom"
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/cams_tempo_by_sector.yaml"
      # When enabled, per-sector speciation splits lumped VOC into mechanism species.

    # Diurnal variation
    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global_per_sector"       # or "regional_per_sector" (wishlist)
      profile_file: "diurnal/olivier_2003.yaml"   # 24 hourly factors per sector

    # Vertical distribution of point sources
    vertical_distribution:
      enabled: false
      # When enabled:
      # profile_file: "vertical/nei_point_sources.yaml"
      # fallback: "surface"           # used where profile is undefined

  # Inventory combining: declare a second source and let category/hierarchy
  # arbitrate overlap (higher hierarchy wins within the same category).
  - name: "nei_us_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../nei-2020"
    file_pattern: "NEI_2020_{YYYY}{MM}{DD}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"
    species_map: "nei_to_mozart"
    category: 1        # same category as CAMS → compared by hierarchy
    hierarchy: 2       # NEI wins over CAMS where both are defined (US domain)
    sectors: [...]
    # ... (same structure as above)
```

### 3. Biomass burning section (`sources/biomass_burning.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "finn_2.6"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "biomass_burning"

    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../finn-2.6"
    file_pattern: "FINN_{YYYY}{DDD}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"
    species: ["CO", "NO", "NMVOC", "PM2.5", ...]
    species_map: "finn_to_mozart"

    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "finn_ratios"            # FINN-native speciation by biome/fuel
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/finn_mozart_t1.yaml"
      # Future: method: "neiva" once integration exists.

    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global"                   # UPTEMPO-style single profile for fires
      profile_file: "diurnal/uptempo_fire.yaml"
      hourly_factors_inline:           # allow override inline (per notes)
        - [0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.15,
           0.14, 0.12, 0.09, 0.07, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02, 0.01,
           0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005]
      regional_override:
        enabled: false
        # file: "diurnal/thailand_local.nc"   # spatial mask + hourly factors

    vertical_distribution:
      mode: "online_plumerise"         # default — plumerise runs in-model
      # mode: "offline_3d"             # read precomputed 3D fire emissions
      # file_pattern: "FINN_3D_{YYYY}{DDD}.nc"
      # QUACS hook: users can swap in their own plumerise parameterization.
```

### 4. Biogenic (`sources/biogenic.yaml`) — offline *or* online

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "megan_online"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "biogenic"

  #   type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
  #   category_type: "biogenic"
  #   mode: "offline"
  #   input_directory: ...
  #   file_pattern: ...
  #   species_map: ...
```

    species_map: "dust_to_mozart"

    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "sea_salt"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.seasalt"

  - name: "lightning_nox"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"

- `include/miem/config.hpp`, `src/config.cpp` — extend schema to accept `micm_config`, `miem-files`, typed `miem-data` entries, `voc_speciation`, `diurnal`, `vertical_distribution`, `mode`, `provider`, `category_type`.
- `include/miem/species_map.hpp` — already structurally adequate; re-type wrapping into `type: SPECIES_MAP`.
- `configs/example_miem.yaml` — migrate to the new schema as a worked example.
- `docs/` — add `miem-config-1.0.md` alongside `ses-1.0.md`.
- A new lightweight MICM config reader (just for species list extraction) — parse `camp-data` entries with `type: CHEM_SPEC`.

## Open Questions for the User

Per Phase 3, flagging decisions that should be confirmed before implementation:

1. **Embed vs. reference:** Plan recommends MIEM as a separate manifest that *references* the MICM config. Alternative is a single combined file with both `camp-data` and `miem-data` arrays. Confirm preference.
2. **`miem-files` vs reusing `camp-files`:** If the community wants a single include mechanism, MIEM entries could be carried inside `camp-files:` lists with distinct `type:` values. This lets MusicBox, QUACS, etc. use one loader. Tradeoff: MICM must ignore unknown types.
3. **VOC speciation method enum:** Current draft lists `cams_tempo`, `finn_ratios`, `custom`. Should `neiva` be a named method now as a forward-looking stub?
4. **Regional diurnal override format:** `profile_file` + optional `regional_override.file` (NetCDF mask) — or a single NetCDF that carries both default and regional? NEI/SMOKE compatibility may dictate.

## Development Isolation

All implementation work for this config-schema change must be done in a **separate git worktree on a dedicated feature branch** (e.g. `feature/miem-config-schema`), branched off `main`. Rationale: the current branch (`feature/scaffolding`) is already carrying in-progress design exploration, and the config-schema change touches public headers, example configs, and docs — it should land as its own reviewable PR without entanglement. Use `git worktree add` so the existing working tree stays untouched while this work proceeds.

  # Vertical distribution profile for NEI point sources.
  # `layers` defines pressure bins (Pa above surface) and the fraction of the
  # point-source mass injected into each bin. Values must sum to 1.0 per sector.
  # Modeled after EPA_ANTHRO_EMIS NEI → WRF-Chem mapping.
  - name: "nei_point_sources"
    type: "VERTICAL_PROFILE"
    coordinate: "pressure_above_surface_pa"
    layers:
      - { bottom: 0,     top: 1000,   fraction: 0.20 }
      - { bottom: 1000,  top: 2500,   fraction: 0.35 }
      - { bottom: 2500,  top: 5000,   fraction: 0.25 }
      - { bottom: 5000,  top: 10000,  fraction: 0.15 }
      - { bottom: 10000, top: 20000,  fraction: 0.05 }
    # Optional: per-sector override. If present, takes precedence over the
    # global `layers:` above for the named sector.
    # per_sector:
    #   point:    [ ... ]
    #   onroad:   [ { bottom: 0, top: 500, fraction: 1.0 } ]

# MIEM Example Config — v1.0 Preliminary Design

This bundle is a hand-authored sample of the MIEM configuration schema
described in the design plan. It is intended for review with Kyle (model
independence), Claire/Louisa (VOC speciation methods), and the broader MUSICA
team before any C++ loader changes are made.

## Layout

```
configs/example/
├── miem.yaml                          # top-level MIEM manifest (entry point)
├── mechanism/
│   ├── config.yaml                    # MICM/CAMP mechanism (referenced by miem.yaml)
│   └── species.yaml                   # abbreviated MOZART-T1 species list
├── sources/
│   ├── anthropogenic.yaml             # CAMS (global) + NEI (US overlay)
│   ├── biomass_burning.yaml           # FINN 2.6
│   ├── biogenic.yaml                  # MEGAN online (+ offline example, commented)
│   └── online_interfaces.yaml         # dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx (QUACS)
├── species_maps/
│   ├── cams_to_mozart.yaml
│   ├── nei_to_mozart.yaml
│   ├── finn_to_mozart.yaml
│   ├── megan_to_mozart.yaml
│   └── quacs_to_mozart.yaml
└── profiles/
    ├── diurnal.yaml                   # Olivier 2003 sectoral + UPTEMPO fire
    ├── voc_speciation.yaml            # CAMS-TEMPO / NEI-SAPRAC / FINN ratios
    └── vertical.yaml                  # NEI point-source vertical profile
```

## Schema conventions (CAMP-aligned)

- Every included file exposes a flat `miem-data:` array of typed entries.
- Each entry has `name:` and `type:`; known types in v1:
  - `EMISSION_SOURCE`, `SPECIES_MAP`, `DIURNAL_PROFILE`, `VOC_PROFILE`, `VERTICAL_PROFILE`.
- Cross-references are by `name:` (e.g. `species_map: "cams_to_mozart"` resolves to the `SPECIES_MAP` entry with that name).
- Mechanism species are discovered by walking `miem.micm_config` → `camp-files:` → `CHEM_SPEC` entries.
- Inventory overlap is resolved HEMCO-style: same `category:` → higher `hierarchy:` wins per cell/species; different `category:` → sum.

## Priorities

- **v1 (this design):** anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (online + offline), online interfaces (dust/sea-salt/lightning).
- **Wishlist:** regional per-sector diurnal profiles; `neiva` VOC speciation; 3D fire emissions read-in path.

## Open questions

See the `## Open Questions for the User` section of the plan at
`/Users/vweeks/.claude/plans/sprightly-popping-salamander.md`.

# MIEM YAML Config Structure — Preliminary Design

## Context

MIEM (Model Independent Emissions Module) needs a YAML configuration format that:

1. **Matches MICM's stylistic conventions** so both configs feel native within the MUSICA ecosystem.
2. **References the MICM config** to discover the set of chemical species the host mechanism requires, then maps inventory species → mechanism species.
3. **Covers all emission source categories** from the user's draft notes: anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (offline/online), dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx. Anthropogenic and biomass burning are the highest-priority sections; online modules (dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx, online biogenic/MEGAN) are interface-only — MIEM receives fluxes rather than computing them.

The existing MIEM scaffolding already supports a subset of this (`configs/example_miem.yaml` with a `miem:` namespace, sources with `type`, `file_pattern`, `species_map`, category/hierarchy aggregation, per-source `scaling_factor`). The new design extends that scaffolding to cover the full v1 feature set while aligning with CAMP-style conventions used by MICM.

## Reference: MICM (CAMP) Config Style

From `NCAR/micm` (`test/tutorial/configs/rate_constants_no_user_defined/`):

```yaml
# config.yaml — include-based entry point
camp-files:
  - species.yaml

## Addendum: Local Config Explorer (HTML artifact)

### Context
Reviewers will evaluate the preliminary design in a meeting. A single-file,
local HTML explorer makes it easier to talk through 15 YAML files than
flipping between files in a terminal. Scope: **local-only**, opened by
double-clicking — not pushed to the repo, not required to work for remote
reviewers. If the design survives review, we can decide later whether it's
worth hosting or shipping alongside the configs.

### Deliverable
A single self-contained HTML file at
`/Users/vweeks/NCAR/ACOM/CheMPAS/MIEM-config-schema/configs/example/explorer.html`
(uncommitted; added to local `.gitignore` or just left untracked). No build
step, no runtime dependencies, no network fetches — the YAML contents of all
15 files are embedded as JavaScript string literals at the top of the file.

### Features (scoped to what adds discussion value)

1. **Left pane — file tree** grouped by directory (`mechanism/`, `sources/`,
   `species_maps/`, `profiles/`, and top-level `miem.yaml`). Click selects a
   file.
2. **Right pane — file viewer** showing the YAML with lightweight syntax
   highlighting (keys, strings, numbers, comments, list markers). Plain regex
   colorization; no third-party library.
3. **Cross-reference jumps** — the key insight. Rewrite these tokens as
   clickable links that select the target file and scroll to the anchor:
   - `species_map: "NAME"` → jumps to the `SPECIES_MAP` entry named NAME.
   - `profile: "NAME"` → jumps to the matching `DIURNAL_PROFILE` /
     `VOC_PROFILE` / `VERTICAL_PROFILE` entry.
   - `micm_config: "./path"` → jumps to `mechanism/config.yaml`.
   - Entries in `miem-files:` / `camp-files:` lists → jump to that included
     file.
4. **Top header — schema legend** listing the five `miem-data` entry types
   (`EMISSION_SOURCE`, `SPECIES_MAP`, `DIURNAL_PROFILE`, `VOC_PROFILE`,
   `VERTICAL_PROFILE`) with a one-line gloss for each, plus counts ("3
   EMISSION_SOURCE entries defined in 2 files"). Counts are computed at
   runtime by scanning the embedded YAML strings.
5. **Quick tour / "reviewer tips" panel** — a collapsible summary of the
   three design decisions that were confirmed via AskUserQuestion, so the
   reviewer doesn't need to read the full plan file.

### Deliberately out of scope
- No full YAML parser. We use regex rewriting on the raw text, which keeps
  the file small and the implementation readable. The MIT-licensed
  `js-yaml` would work but adds ~60KB; not worth it for a temporary
  discussion aid.
- No diff view against the existing `configs/example_miem.yaml`.
- No edit capability. View-only.
- No dark/light toggle, no responsive mobile layout. Desktop browser, one
  theme (dark), one window.

### Files to create
- `configs/example/explorer.html` — the artifact. ~400 lines, single file.

### Verification
- Open with `open configs/example/explorer.html` from the worktree.
- Click every file in the left pane; confirm content renders.
- Click a `species_map: "cams_to_mozart"` reference in
  `sources/anthropogenic.yaml`; confirm it navigates to
  `species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml` and highlights the target entry.
- Confirm header counts match the design (e.g. 5 EMISSION_SOURCE entries
  across 4 files after counting CAMS, NEI, FINN, MEGAN online, and the 3
  online-interface entries — so actually 7).

## Development Isolation

# MIEM YAML Config Structure — Preliminary Design

## Context

MIEM (Model Independent Emissions Module) needs a YAML configuration format that:

1. **Matches MICM's stylistic conventions** so both configs feel native within the MUSICA ecosystem.
2. **References the MICM config** to discover the set of chemical species the host mechanism requires, then maps inventory species → mechanism species.
3. **Covers all emission source categories** from the user's draft notes: anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (offline/online), dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx. Anthropogenic and biomass burning are the highest-priority sections; online modules (dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx, online biogenic/MEGAN) are interface-only — MIEM receives fluxes rather than computing them.

The existing MIEM scaffolding already supports a subset of this (`configs/example_miem.yaml` with a `miem:` namespace, sources with `type`, `file_pattern`, `species_map`, category/hierarchy aggregation, per-source `scaling_factor`). The new design extends that scaffolding to cover the full v1 feature set while aligning with CAMP-style conventions used by MICM.

## Reference: MICM (CAMP) Config Style

From `NCAR/micm` (`test/tutorial/configs/rate_constants_no_user_defined/`):

```yaml
# config.yaml — include-based entry point
camp-files:
  - species.yaml
  - reactions.yaml
```

```yaml
# species.yaml — typed, flat list of entries
camp-data:
  - name: "NO"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
    molecular weight [kg mol-1]: 0.030
  - name: "ISOP"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
```

Key stylistic traits to adopt:

- Top-level `camp-files:` as an include manifest (MIEM can add `miem-files:` analog, or reuse the same pattern).
- Entries live in a `camp-data:` array, each with `name:` and `type:` and arbitrary typed fields.
- Units embedded in key names using square brackets (`molecular weight [kg mol-1]`).
- YAML and JSON are interchangeable.

## Design Decision: MIEM as a Parallel Manifest

**Recommendation:** Keep MIEM's configuration in its **own top-level manifest file** (not inlined into the MICM config), but have the MIEM manifest carry a `micm_config:` reference so MIEM can parse MICM's species list at load time.

Rationale:
- Keeps the MICM file purely a chemistry description — usable standalone by MusicBox and other clients that don't need emissions.
- Matches the meeting-note preference ("Or it could be a GUI tool [QUACS] that reads the MICM file to generate the MIEM config").
- Avoids schema drift: MICM stays CAMP-pure; MIEM declares its own `miem-data` typed entries in the same style.

## Preliminary YAML Design

### 1. Top-level manifest (`miem.yaml`)

```yaml
miem:
  version: "1.0"

  # Points to the MICM/CAMP config so MIEM can query the mechanism species list.
  # MIEM reads this at startup to (a) know which species it must provide fluxes for,
  # and (b) validate that every mapping target exists in the mechanism.
  micm_config: "./mechanism/config.yaml"
  mechanism_name: "MOZART-T1"   # informational; cross-checked against MICM file

  # Include manifest, CAMP-style. Each included file contributes miem-data entries.
  miem-files:
    - sources/anthropogenic.yaml
    - sources/biomass_burning.yaml
    - sources/biogenic.yaml
    - online_interfaces.yaml
    - species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml
    - species_maps/finn_to_mozart.yaml
```

### 2. Anthropogenic section (`sources/anthropogenic.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "cams_global_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"

    # I/O
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../cams-v6.2"
    file_pattern: "CAMS-GLOB-ANT_v6.2_{YYYY}{MM}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"            # or "custom" → requires descriptor:
    # descriptor: { variable_prefix: "emi_", flux_units: "kg m-2 s-1", ... }

    # Species
    species: ["NO", "NO2", "CO", "SO2", "NH3", "VOC_total"]
    species_map: "cams_to_mozart"    # references a SPECIES_MAP entry by name

    # Sectors & aggregation (HEMCO-style)
    process_sectors: true
    sectors: ["energy", "industry", "transport", "residential", "agriculture"]
    category: 1
    hierarchy: 1
    scaling_factor: 1.0

    # VOC speciation
    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "cams_tempo"            # or "finn_ratios", "custom"
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/cams_tempo_by_sector.yaml"
      # When enabled, per-sector speciation splits lumped VOC into mechanism species.

    # Diurnal variation
    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global_per_sector"       # or "regional_per_sector" (wishlist)
      profile_file: "diurnal/olivier_2003.yaml"   # 24 hourly factors per sector

    # Vertical distribution of point sources
    vertical_distribution:
      enabled: false
      # When enabled:
      # profile_file: "vertical/nei_point_sources.yaml"
      # fallback: "surface"           # used where profile is undefined

  # Inventory combining: declare a second source and let category/hierarchy
  # arbitrate overlap (higher hierarchy wins within the same category).
  - name: "nei_us_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../nei-2020"
    file_pattern: "NEI_2020_{YYYY}{MM}{DD}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"
    species_map: "nei_to_mozart"
    category: 1        # same category as CAMS → compared by hierarchy
    hierarchy: 2       # NEI wins over CAMS where both are defined (US domain)
    sectors: [...]
    # ... (same structure as above)
```

### 3. Biomass burning section (`sources/biomass_burning.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "finn_2.6"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "biomass_burning"

    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../finn-2.6"
    file_pattern: "FINN_{YYYY}{DDD}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"
    species: ["CO", "NO", "NMVOC", "PM2.5", ...]
    species_map: "finn_to_mozart"

    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "finn_ratios"            # FINN-native speciation by biome/fuel
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/finn_mozart_t1.yaml"
      # Future: method: "neiva" once integration exists.

    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global"                   # UPTEMPO-style single profile for fires
      profile_file: "diurnal/uptempo_fire.yaml"
      hourly_factors_inline:           # allow override inline (per notes)
        - [0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.15,
           0.14, 0.12, 0.09, 0.07, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02, 0.01,
           0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005]
      regional_override:
        enabled: false
        # file: "diurnal/thailand_local.nc"   # spatial mask + hourly factors

    vertical_distribution:
      mode: "online_plumerise"         # default — plumerise runs in-model
      # mode: "offline_3d"             # read precomputed 3D fire emissions
      # file_pattern: "FINN_3D_{YYYY}{DDD}.nc"
      # QUACS hook: users can swap in their own plumerise parameterization.
```

### 4. Biogenic (`sources/biogenic.yaml`) — offline *or* online

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "megan_online"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "biogenic"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "megan"                 # code lives outside MIEM (QUACS-managed)
    # MIEM only receives fluxes from this provider and forwards them.
    species_map: "megan_to_mozart"
    # Optional: whether MIEM should stage MEGAN input datasets:
    stage_inputs: false
    # If true: MIEM reads land-use from host static fields rather than MODIS.
    use_host_landuse: true

  # Alternative offline form — structurally identical to anthropogenic:
  # - name: "megan_offline_climo"
  #   type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
  #   category_type: "biogenic"
  #   mode: "offline"
  #   input_directory: ...
  #   file_pattern: ...
  #   species_map: ...
```

### 5. Online-only interface sources (`online_interfaces.yaml`)

Dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx — MIEM is a pass-through that collects fluxes computed by external (QUACS-managed) modules.

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "dust_online"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "dust"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.dust"            # QUACS-provided scheme name
    species_map: "dust_to_mozart"

  - name: "seasalt_online"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "sea_salt"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.seasalt"
    species_map: "seasalt_to_mozart"

  - name: "lightning_nox"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "lightning_nox"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.lightning"
    species_map: "lightning_to_mozart"
```

### 6. Species maps (`species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml`)

Reuses the existing `SpeciesMap` structure already present in the code
(`include/miem/species_map.hpp`), re-typed as a `miem-data` entry for consistency:

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "cams_to_mozart"
    type: "SPECIES_MAP"
    mechanism: "MOZART-T1"
    mappings:
      - inventory: "NOx"
        mechanism: "NO"
        scaling: 0.9
      - inventory: "NOx"
        mechanism: "NO2"
        scaling: 0.1
      - inventory: "CO"
        mechanism: "CO"
    # Species present in the MICM mechanism but absent from mappings are flagged
    # at load time — echoes the meeting note "informs that none exists and
    # requires user input".
```

### 7. Diurnal / VOC / vertical profile files

These are small standalone YAML files referenced by the source entries — also
`miem-data` typed, for include-compatibility:

```yaml
# diurnal/olivier_2003.yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "olivier_2003_diurnal"
    type: "DIURNAL_PROFILE"
    sectors:
      energy:       [0.03, 0.03, ...24 values]
      transport:    [0.01, 0.01, ...]
      residential:  [...]
```

## Critical Files to Modify (when implementation begins)

Design-only task now; listing for downstream work:

- `include/miem/config.hpp`, `src/config.cpp` — extend schema to accept `micm_config`, `miem-files`, typed `miem-data` entries, `voc_speciation`, `diurnal`, `vertical_distribution`, `mode`, `provider`, `category_type`.
- `include/miem/species_map.hpp` — already structurally adequate; re-type wrapping into `type: SPECIES_MAP`.
- `configs/example_miem.yaml` — migrate to the new schema as a worked example.
- `docs/` — add `miem-config-1.0.md` alongside `ses-1.0.md`.
- A new lightweight MICM config reader (just for species list extraction) — parse `camp-data` entries with `type: CHEM_SPEC`.

## Open Questions for the User

Per Phase 3, flagging decisions that should be confirmed before implementation:

1. **Embed vs. reference:** Plan recommends MIEM as a separate manifest that *references* the MICM config. Alternative is a single combined file with both `camp-data` and `miem-data` arrays. Confirm preference.
2. **`miem-files` vs reusing `camp-files`:** If the community wants a single include mechanism, MIEM entries could be carried inside `camp-files:` lists with distinct `type:` values. This lets MusicBox, QUACS, etc. use one loader. Tradeoff: MICM must ignore unknown types.
3. **VOC speciation method enum:** Current draft lists `cams_tempo`, `finn_ratios`, `custom`. Should `neiva` be a named method now as a forward-looking stub?
4. **Regional diurnal override format:** `profile_file` + optional `regional_override.file` (NetCDF mask) — or a single NetCDF that carries both default and regional? NEI/SMOKE compatibility may dictate.

# MIEM YAML Config Structure — Preliminary Design

## Context

MIEM (Model Independent Emissions Module) needs a YAML configuration format that:

1. **Matches MICM's stylistic conventions** so both configs feel native within the MUSICA ecosystem.
2. **References the MICM config** to discover the set of chemical species the host mechanism requires, then maps inventory species → mechanism species.
3. **Covers all emission source categories** from the user's draft notes: anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (offline/online), dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx. Anthropogenic and biomass burning are the highest-priority sections; online modules (dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx, online biogenic/MEGAN) are interface-only — MIEM receives fluxes rather than computing them.

The existing MIEM scaffolding already supports a subset of this (`configs/example_miem.yaml` with a `miem:` namespace, sources with `type`, `file_pattern`, `species_map`, category/hierarchy aggregation, per-source `scaling_factor`). The new design extends that scaffolding to cover the full v1 feature set while aligning with CAMP-style conventions used by MICM.

## Reference: MICM (CAMP) Config Style

From `NCAR/micm` (`test/tutorial/configs/rate_constants_no_user_defined/`):

```yaml
# config.yaml — include-based entry point
camp-files:
  - species.yaml
  - reactions.yaml
```

```yaml
# species.yaml — typed, flat list of entries
camp-data:
  - name: "NO"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
    molecular weight [kg mol-1]: 0.030
  - name: "ISOP"
    type: "CHEM_SPEC"
```

Key stylistic traits to adopt:

- Top-level `camp-files:` as an include manifest (MIEM can add `miem-files:` analog, or reuse the same pattern).
- Entries live in a `camp-data:` array, each with `name:` and `type:` and arbitrary typed fields.
- Units embedded in key names using square brackets (`molecular weight [kg mol-1]`).
- YAML and JSON are interchangeable.

## Design Decision: MIEM as a Parallel Manifest

**Recommendation:** Keep MIEM's configuration in its **own top-level manifest file** (not inlined into the MICM config), but have the MIEM manifest carry a `micm_config:` reference so MIEM can parse MICM's species list at load time.

Rationale:
- Keeps the MICM file purely a chemistry description — usable standalone by MusicBox and other clients that don't need emissions.
- Matches the meeting-note preference ("Or it could be a GUI tool [QUACS] that reads the MICM file to generate the MIEM config").
- Avoids schema drift: MICM stays CAMP-pure; MIEM declares its own `miem-data` typed entries in the same style.

## Preliminary YAML Design

### 1. Top-level manifest (`miem.yaml`)

```yaml
miem:
  version: "1.0"

  # Points to the MICM/CAMP config so MIEM can query the mechanism species list.
  # MIEM reads this at startup to (a) know which species it must provide fluxes for,
  # and (b) validate that every mapping target exists in the mechanism.
  micm_config: "./mechanism/config.yaml"
  mechanism_name: "MOZART-T1"   # informational; cross-checked against MICM file

  # Include manifest, CAMP-style. Each included file contributes miem-data entries.
  miem-files:
    - sources/anthropogenic.yaml
    - sources/biomass_burning.yaml
    - sources/biogenic.yaml
    - online_interfaces.yaml
    - species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml
    - species_maps/finn_to_mozart.yaml
```

### 2. Anthropogenic section (`sources/anthropogenic.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "cams_global_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"

    # I/O
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../cams-v6.2"
    file_pattern: "CAMS-GLOB-ANT_v6.2_{YYYY}{MM}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"            # or "custom" → requires descriptor:
    # descriptor: { variable_prefix: "emi_", flux_units: "kg m-2 s-1", ... }

    # Species
    species: ["NO", "NO2", "CO", "SO2", "NH3", "VOC_total"]
    species_map: "cams_to_mozart"    # references a SPECIES_MAP entry by name

    # Sectors & aggregation (HEMCO-style)
    process_sectors: true
    sectors: ["energy", "industry", "transport", "residential", "agriculture"]
    category: 1
    hierarchy: 1
    scaling_factor: 1.0

    # VOC speciation
    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "cams_tempo"            # or "finn_ratios", "custom"
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/cams_tempo_by_sector.yaml"
      # When enabled, per-sector speciation splits lumped VOC into mechanism species.

    # Diurnal variation
    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global_per_sector"       # or "regional_per_sector" (wishlist)
      profile_file: "diurnal/olivier_2003.yaml"   # 24 hourly factors per sector

    # Vertical distribution of point sources
    vertical_distribution:
      enabled: false
      # When enabled:
      # profile_file: "vertical/nei_point_sources.yaml"
      # fallback: "surface"           # used where profile is undefined

  # Inventory combining: declare a second source and let category/hierarchy
  # arbitrate overlap (higher hierarchy wins within the same category).
  - name: "nei_us_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"
    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../nei-2020"
    file_pattern: "NEI_2020_{YYYY}{MM}{DD}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"
    species_map: "nei_to_mozart"
    category: 1        # same category as CAMS → compared by hierarchy
    hierarchy: 2       # NEI wins over CAMS where both are defined (US domain)
    sectors: [...]
    # ... (same structure as above)
```

### 3. Biomass burning section (`sources/biomass_burning.yaml`) — Priority 1

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "finn_2.6"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "biomass_burning"

    input_directory: "/glade/work/.../finn-2.6"
    file_pattern: "FINN_{YYYY}{DDD}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"
    species: ["CO", "NO", "NMVOC", "PM2.5", ...]
    species_map: "finn_to_mozart"

    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "finn_ratios"            # FINN-native speciation by biome/fuel
      profile_file: "voc_profiles/finn_mozart_t1.yaml"
      # Future: method: "neiva" once integration exists.

    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global"                   # UPTEMPO-style single profile for fires
      profile_file: "diurnal/uptempo_fire.yaml"
      hourly_factors_inline:           # allow override inline (per notes)
        - [0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.15,
           0.14, 0.12, 0.09, 0.07, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02, 0.01,
           0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005, 0.005]
      regional_override:
        enabled: false
        # file: "diurnal/thailand_local.nc"   # spatial mask + hourly factors

    vertical_distribution:
      mode: "online_plumerise"         # default — plumerise runs in-model
      # mode: "offline_3d"             # read precomputed 3D fire emissions
      # file_pattern: "FINN_3D_{YYYY}{DDD}.nc"
      # QUACS hook: users can swap in their own plumerise parameterization.
```

### 4. Biogenic (`sources/biogenic.yaml`) — offline *or* online

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "megan_online"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "biogenic"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "megan"                 # code lives outside MIEM (QUACS-managed)
    # MIEM only receives fluxes from this provider and forwards them.
    species_map: "megan_to_mozart"
    # Optional: whether MIEM should stage MEGAN input datasets:
    stage_inputs: false
    # If true: MIEM reads land-use from host static fields rather than MODIS.
    use_host_landuse: true

  # Alternative offline form — structurally identical to anthropogenic:
  # - name: "megan_offline_climo"
  #   type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
  #   category_type: "biogenic"
  #   mode: "offline"
  #   input_directory: ...
  #   file_pattern: ...
  #   species_map: ...
```

### 5. Online-only interface sources (`online_interfaces.yaml`)

Dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx — MIEM is a pass-through that collects fluxes computed by external (QUACS-managed) modules.

```yaml
miem-data:
  - name: "dust_online"

    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.dust"            # QUACS-provided scheme name

  - name: "lightning_nox"

    category_type: "lightning_nox"
    mode: "online"
    provider: "quacs.lightning"
    species_map: "lightning_to_mozart"
```

### 6. Species maps (`species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml`)

Reuses the existing `SpeciesMap` structure already present in the code

```

These are small standalone YAML files referenced by the source entries — also

```yaml

content.text: `★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────` The root cause is a classic "don't chain regex replaces on string output you just wrote to" mistake. The first pass wrote `...`, the second pass (`/"[^"]*"/g` for strings) then matched the `"key"` attribute value inside that tag and wrapped it again, producing `"key">...`. The browser treats the malformed `` as an invalid tag, drops the prefix, and leaves the literal text `"key">` visible. The fix separates **structural** tokens (leading whitespace, optional `- `, optional `KEY:`) from **value** tokens (strings/numbers/booleans) and only tokenizes the value portion, which is guaranteed to contain no previously-emitted HTML. `─────────────────────────────────────────────────` Refresh the browser window. Every line should now render correctly: - **Yellow** keys (`miem:`, `version:`, etc.) - **Green** quoted strings (`"1.0"`, `"MOZART-T1"`) - **Dashed blue links** on cross-references and include paths - **Purple** numbers (`0.030`, `1.0`) - **Slate italic** comments Try clicking `"cams_to_mozart"` on the anthropogenic page — it should jump to the `SPECIES_MAP` entry in `species_maps/cams_to_mozart.yaml`.

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is a meaningful axis choice: files-per-source vs. files-per-mechanism. The trade-off is about which dimension changes more often — **mechanisms are stable** (MOZART-T1 has been the standard for years), while **inventories churn** (new CAMS releases every couple years). By that logic, per-mechanism grouping colocates things that change together and separates things that change independently, which is usually the right instinct. But the bigger design question is whether "source nested in mechanism" means keeping one `SPECIES_MAP` entry per source (just moved into a shared file) or collapsing into **one `SPECIES_MAP` per mechanism** with a `sources:` sub-map. Those look different to the loader, and source entries reference them differently.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Before I implement, two shape options — they change what the entry looks like and how sources reference it.

content.text:
What would you like to clarify about the per-mechanism species-map shape? For context, the three options differ on:

1. **Option 1** — cosmetic only: today's structure (one `SPECIES_MAP` entry per inventory), just all grouped into one file per mechanism. No changes to loader or source references.
2. **Option 2** — a single `SPECIES_MAP` entry per mechanism with a `sources:` sub-map. Source entries reference the mechanism-level entry plus a source key.
3. **Option 3** — same as Option 2, but source references use just the source tag (e.g. `species_map: "cams"`); the loader resolves the active mechanism implicitly since MIEM runs against one MICM config at a time.

Happy to walk through any of them in more detail, or explore a shape I haven't mentioned. What's the concern or question driving the reformulation?

message.content: For option number 2, if we were to add a different anthro like SEDS, what would it look like?

content.text:
Good concrete question. Adding SEDS under Option 2 touches exactly two places:

**1. The mechanism file — add a new key under `sources:`**

```yaml
# species_maps/mozart_t1.yaml  (before/after)
miem-data:
  - name: "mozart_t1"
    type: "SPECIES_MAP"
    mechanism: "MOZART-T1"
    sources:
      cams:
        - inventory: "NOx"
          mechanism: "NO"
          scaling: 0.9
        ...
      nei:
        - inventory: "NO"
          mechanism: "NO"
        ...
      finn:
        ...
      megan:
        ...

      # ── new ─────────────────────────────────
      seds:
        - inventory: "NOx"
          mechanism: "NO"
          scaling: 0.9
        - inventory: "NOx"
          mechanism: "NO2"
          scaling: 0.1
        - inventory: "CO"
          mechanism: "CO"
        - inventory: "SO2"
          mechanism: "SO2"
        - inventory: "BC_fossil"
          mechanism: "BC"
        - inventory: "BC_biofuel"
          mechanism: "BC"
        - inventory: "OC_fossil"
          mechanism: "OC"
        - inventory: "OC_biofuel"
          mechanism: "OC"
      # ────────────────────────────────────────
```

**2. The anthropogenic sources file — a new `EMISSION_SOURCE` entry**

```yaml
# sources/anthropogenic.yaml  (appended)
miem-data:
  ...existing cams_global_anthro, nei_us_anthro entries...

  - name: "seds_global_anthro"
    type: "EMISSION_SOURCE"
    category_type: "anthropogenic"
    mode: "offline"

    input_directory: "/glade/campaign/acom/emissions/seds-v1"
    file_pattern: "SEDS_{YYYY}.nc"
    convention: "SES-1.0"

    species: ["NOx", "CO", "SO2", "BC_fossil", "BC_biofuel", "OC_fossil", "OC_biofuel"]

    species_map:
      mechanism: "mozart_t1"
      source: "seds"

    process_sectors: true
    sectors: ["energy", "industry", "transport", "residential", "agriculture"]
    category: 1        # same as CAMS/NEI → arbitrated by hierarchy
    hierarchy: 3       # above NEI where SEDS has coverage, or drop lower
    scaling_factor: 1.0

    voc_speciation:
      enabled: true
      method: "cams_tempo"
      profile: "cams_tempo_sector_split"

    diurnal:
      enabled: true
      mode: "global_per_sector"
      profile: "olivier_2003"

    vertical_distribution:
      enabled: false
```

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Two things worth calling out about this shape: (1) The **compound reference** `species_map: {mechanism: ..., source: ...}` is what makes Option 2 different from Option 3 — it's more verbose at the source site but preserves uniqueness when two mechanisms both define a source called `cams`. (2) Adding SEDS still means **editing two files**, same as today's per-inventory design; the difference is *which* second file. In Option 2 you edit the mechanism file (you want to support this inventory for mozart_t1); in the current design you create a brand new `species_maps/seds_to_mozart.yaml`. Option 2 forces you to also think "does this also need mappings for CB6, SAPRC, etc." when you add an inventory — which is arguably the right prompt, because a new inventory that only works with one mechanism is a red flag.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

One wrinkle to flag: if SEDS needs to be supported for multiple mechanisms (say MOZART-T1 *and* CB6), you'd add a `seds:` block under each mechanism's file. The repetition is real, but it's also honest — the mappings themselves differ per mechanism (CB6 has different species names like `HNO3`, `PAR`, `OLE`), so the duplication isn't accidental.

Want me to re-run the original question with this concrete example in mind, or is there more to clarify before I implement?

# MIEM Example Config — v1.0 Preliminary Design

This bundle is a hand-authored sample of the MIEM configuration schema
described in the design plan. It is intended for review with Kyle (model
independence), Claire/Louisa (VOC speciation methods), and the broader MUSICA
team before any C++ loader changes are made.

## Layout

```
configs/example/
├── miem.yaml                          # top-level MIEM manifest (entry point)
├── mechanism/
│   ├── config.yaml                    # MICM/CAMP mechanism (referenced by miem.yaml)
│   └── species.yaml                   # abbreviated MOZART-T1 species list
├── sources/
│   ├── anthropogenic.yaml             # CAMS (global) + NEI (US overlay)
│   ├── biomass_burning.yaml           # FINN 2.6
│   ├── biogenic.yaml                  # MEGAN online (+ offline example, commented)
│   └── online_interfaces.yaml         # dust, sea-salt, lightning NOx (QUACS)
├── species_maps/
│   ├── cams_to_mozart.yaml
│   ├── nei_to_mozart.yaml
│   ├── finn_to_mozart.yaml
│   ├── megan_to_mozart.yaml
│   └── quacs_to_mozart.yaml
└── profiles/
    ├── diurnal.yaml                   # Olivier 2003 sectoral + UPTEMPO fire
    ├── voc_speciation.yaml            # CAMS-TEMPO / NEI-SAPRAC / FINN ratios
    └── vertical.yaml                  # NEI point-source vertical profile
```

## Schema conventions (CAMP-aligned)

- Every included file exposes a flat `miem-data:` array of typed entries.
- Each entry has `name:` and `type:`; known types in v1:
  - `EMISSION_SOURCE`, `SPECIES_MAP`, `DIURNAL_PROFILE`, `VOC_PROFILE`, `VERTICAL_PROFILE`.
- Cross-references are by `name:` (e.g. `species_map: "cams_to_mozart"` resolves to the `SPECIES_MAP` entry with that name).
- Mechanism species are discovered by walking `miem.micm_config` → `camp-files:` → `CHEM_SPEC` entries.
- Inventory overlap is resolved HEMCO-style: same `category:` → higher `hierarchy:` wins per cell/species; different `category:` → sum.

## Priorities

- **v1 (this design):** anthropogenic, biomass burning, biogenic (online + offline), online interfaces (dust/sea-salt/lightning).
- **Wishlist:** regional per-sector diurnal profiles; `neiva` VOC speciation; 3D fire emissions read-in path.

## Open questions

See the `## Open Questions for the User` section of the plan at
`/Users/vweeks/.claude/plans/sprightly-popping-salamander.md`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Two interesting effects worth noticing in the new structure: (1) **Count drops from 5 to 1.** The header chip legend now shows "SPECIES_MAP 1" — because there's just one entry, the one-per-mechanism. This immediately communicates the design intent at a glance. (2) **Source-key lines in `mozart_t1.yaml` become jump targets.** In the registry, I added `SOURCE_REGISTRY[map][srcKey] = {path, line}` alongside the normal registry. When you click `"cams"` in a compound reference, you don't just jump to the file — you jump to the specific `cams:` line inside `sources:`, which makes the per-source block visually distinct even though the file is long. Clicking `"mozart_t1"` jumps to the top of the SPECIES_MAP entry (the `- name: "mozart_t1"` line), so the two halves of the compound reference land at structurally different scopes. That's the discussion value you get from making them clickable separately rather than as one token.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Worktree files (committable):**
- New: `configs/example/species_maps/mozart_t1.yaml` — single SPECIES_MAP with 7 `sources:` keys (cams, nei, finn, megan, dust, seasalt, lightning)
